approachQuestion.prompt:
Covering an exposed cable

A cable segment [L,R] must be covered without any gap by a subset of n available closed protective sleeves [start,end]. Sleeves may overlap or touch and may extend outside the cable. Return the minimum number of sleeves whose union covers [L,R], or −1 if impossible. Sleeves are unsorted and immutable. Return only the count.

Input: L=0, R=10, sleeves=[[0,3],[0,6],[3,7],[6,10]]
Output: 2
Use [0,6] and [6,10].

Input: L=1, R=8, sleeves=[[0,4],[5,9]]
Output: -1

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ L < R ≤ 1000000000; 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 1000000000. Use comparison-based ordering. Choose the best worst-case running time.

options.text: Sort copied sleeves by start. Beginning at L, scan every not-yet-considered sleeve starting at or before the covered frontier and find the farthest end. If it does not advance the frontier, report −1; otherwise choose that extension, increment the count, and repeat until reaching R.
options.feedback: Any next sleeve must begin no later than the covered frontier. Among those, the farthest end leaves every continuation available and can replace a shorter chosen extension without increasing the number used.

options.text: Sort sleeves by end and repeatedly choose the earliest-ending sleeve that starts at or before the frontier and extends it.
options.feedback: For cable [0,10] and sleeves [[0,3],[0,10]], choosing [0,3] first uses 2 sleeves instead of the optimal 1. The scheduling rule for keeping many intervals is unsuitable here.

options.text: At each frontier, rescan the entire original list for sleeves starting at or before it; choose the farthest reachable end, failing if there is no advance.
options.feedback: This finds the correct minimum, but may rescan all sleeves for each of many successive extensions. Keeping a forward index in start order avoids repeated brute-force searches.

options.text: Repeatedly choose the unused sleeve with greatest end, regardless of its start, until some chosen end reaches R.
options.feedback: For cable [0,10] and sleeves [[0,4],[8,10]], this chooses [8,10] and reports success although [4,8] remains uncovered. An extension must connect to coverage already obtained.

feedback.reason: Choose the farthest feasible extension of connected coverage rather than an unrelated interval scheduling heuristic.
details: Copy and sort sleeves by start using iterative bottom-up merge sort with a reusable buffer. Maintain a forward index, frontier and farthest reachable end; each sleeve is scanned once across all choices. Store no chosen-sleeve list because only the count is returned.

Among sleeves starting by the current frontier, choose the farthest end. Any shorter choice cannot improve remaining coverage. If no candidate advances the frontier, expose impossibility instead of accepting a disconnected next sleeve.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For farthest-reachable-extension, n is the sleeve count. Include the copied array and merge buffer. Choose the tightest standard worst-case pair.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)
Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)

feedback.reason: Sort once; the frontier scan never restarts from the first sleeve.
details: Sorting dominates the forward scan with O(n log n) time. The index never restarts, so repeated choices do not create a nested full scan. Copies and the reusable buffer use O(n); the greedy state is constant and iterative.
Comparison merge sort, iterative and buffered; scalar output.
“Time O(n²), auxiliary space O(n)”: The forward index is never restarted for each chosen sleeve. All sleeves are scanned once after sorting.
“Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(1)”: The copy and reusable merge buffer must be counted. Returning only a scalar does not remove those arrays.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(1)”: The unsorted sleeves are comparison-sorted first, with linear auxiliary storage for their copy and buffer.
